title: Add in-app parent confirmation notification when child submits parent phone number

requirements.text: Implement a persistent in-app notification/request flow for phone-based parent-child linking: when a CHILD submits a phone number that matches a PARENT’s registered phone number, create a pending confirmation request addressed to that parent, and block completion of the phone-based pairing until the PARENT confirms with one click.

quotes: ajuste somente: Quando o FILHO cadastra o número, o backend cria uma notificação interna. • O PAI/MÃE recebe um alerta na interface. • O PAI/MÃE confirma com um clique.

acceptanceCriteria: When a child initiates phone pairing with a valid phone number that belongs to a parent, the backend stores a new pending confirmation request tied to (parentId, childId, phoneNumber, createdAt, status).
Pending confirmation requests survive canister upgrades (if the app currently persists state, update migration accordingly per the project’s conditional migration policy).
A child cannot become paired to the parent via phone flow until the parent confirms the request.
Only the addressed parent (and admins, if applicable) can view/act on that confirmation request; other users cannot read or confirm it.
The backend exposes actor methods needed by the UI to (a) create the request (child action), (b) list pending requests for the current parent, and (c) confirm a specific request (parent action).
Confirming a request results in the parent-child link being created and the request marked as confirmed/closed, and the relevant audit log entry is recorded for traceability.

requirements.text: Add a parent-facing UI alert that surfaces pending phone confirmation requests and allows the PARENT to confirm with one click.

quotes: O PAI/MÃE recebe um alerta na interface. • O PAI/MÃE confirma com um clique.

acceptanceCriteria: In the parent experience (e.g., ParentDashboard), if there is at least one pending phone confirmation request for the logged-in parent, the UI displays a clear alert/banner/card indicating a child is requesting to link via phone number.
The alert includes a single primary action to confirm the request; clicking it triggers the backend confirm call and shows a success toast/message on completion.
After confirmation, parent UI updates without a full refresh (React Query invalidation/refetch) and the pending alert disappears.
All new user-facing text added for this feature is in English and wired through the existing i18n system (update the English dictionary at minimum).

requirements.text: Update the child phone pairing UI flow so that after the CHILD submits the parent phone number, the UI reflects “pending parent confirmation” state instead of (or in addition to) the current OTP-based completion step, and keeps polling/refetching until the request is confirmed.

quotes: Quando o FILHO cadastra o número, o backend cria uma notificação interna.

acceptanceCriteria: In the child pairing UI (PairWithParentCard), submitting a phone number that matches a parent creates a pending confirmation request and the UI indicates the request was sent and is awaiting parent confirmation.
The child UI does not require SMS/OTP entry to complete this confirmation flow.
Once the parent confirms, the child UI reflects that pairing is completed (e.g., by refetching useGetMyParent and showing the paired state card).

React Query hooks are added/updated in frontend/src/hooks/useQueries.ts to support creating the request, fetching pending status (as needed), and confirming requests; queries/mutations correctly invalidate existing keys like ['myParent'] and ['myChildren'] after confirmation.

constraints: Do not add SMS sending or any external SMS provider integration.
Do not attempt to keep the web app running after the browser is closed (no always-on background execution requirement).
Backend changes must conform to the single-actor Motoko architecture in backend/main.mo.
Do not modify files under frontend/src/components/ui or other immutable paths listed in SYSTEM_CONTEXT.
nonGoals: Implementing real SMS delivery or OTP via SMS.
Implementing background execution when the browser/app is closed beyond existing PWA/service worker capabilities.
Adding real-time sockets/WebSocket-based notifications (use polling/refetch patterns already in use).
